editorial.headline: On-Street Parking: Open Nationally, Unblocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 52214 covers parking organised on the roadway itself, open to every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally, with no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 52214 is narrowly about the organisation of parking on the street itself: parking carried out within the road body. That focus matters. This is an activity defined by where the parking is conducted, rather than a broad label for every parking-related operation. For a founder shaping a business around managed on-street parking, the code describes the activity at its most direct and physical point of delivery.

The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In practical ownership terms, the record sets no foreign-equity gap below full ownership for this activity at the national level. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that national opening here. The provincial assessment is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the activity is not blocked for PMA registration by Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The reason is specific: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing the activity outside that moratorium block. A foreign investor can therefore register this activity in Bali today under the position reflected in the record.

That is the useful distinction to retain. The national position is fully open to foreign ownership, while the Bali result is also open—not because the provincial moratorium is absent, but because this activity’s recorded risk position at the Besar scale means it is not caught by that rule. For an on-street parking venture, the record offers a clear reading: the activity is available across all listed scales, supports up to 100% foreign ownership nationally, and has no recorded Bali PMA-registration block.
